'''Gregor Eugen Morfill''' (born 23 July 1945 in [[Oberhausen|Oberhausen, Germany]]) is a German physicist who works in [[Astrophysics|basic astrophysical research]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sterzik|first1=Michael F.|last2=Morfill|first2=Gregor E.|date=1994|title=Evolution of Protoplanetary Disks with Condensation and Coagulation|journal=Icarus|volume=111|issue=2|pages=536–546|doi=10.1006/icar.1994.1162|bibcode=1994Icar..111..536S|issn=0019-1035}}</ref> and deals with [[Dusty plasma|complex plasmas]]<ref>{{Citation|last1=Tsytovich|first1=Vadim N.|chapter=Elementary Processes in Complex Plasmas|date=2008|title=Elementary Physics of Complex Plasmas|pages=67–140|publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg|isbn=978-3-642-06703-7|last2=Morfill|first2=Gregory E.|last3=Vladimirov|first3=Sergey V.|last4=Thomas|first4=Hubertus M.|series=Lecture Notes in Physics |volume=731|doi=10.1007/978-3-540-29003-2_3|bibcode=2008LNP...731...67T}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nunomura|first1=S.|last2=Samsonov|first2=D.|last3=Zhdanov|first3=S.|last4=Morfill|first4=G.|date=2005|title=Heat Transfer in a Two-Dimensional Crystalline Complex (Dusty) Plasma|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=95|issue=2|article-number=025003|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.95.025003|pmid=16090692|bibcode=2005PhRvL..95b5003N|issn=0031-9007}}</ref> and [[plasma medicine]].

== Early life and career ==
Gregor Morfill moved to England in 1961. There, he completed his school education and began studying physics at [[Imperial College London]] in 1964. In 1967, he graduated with a Bachelor of Science. In 1968, he received a diploma from [[Imperial College London]] and in 1971 he received a PhD with his work Satellite studies of energetic particles above the atmosphere. He then went to the [[Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics]] in [[Garching bei München|Garching]]. In 1977, he did his [[post-doctorate]] at [[Heidelberg University]].

In 1975, he received a professorship at the [[Max Planck Institute for Nuclear Physics]] in [[Heidelberg]]. In 1983, he headed the Theoretical Astronomy Program at the [[University of Arizona]]. In 1984, he became director of the Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics.

Since 2011, he has been on the scientific advisory board of [[Bauman Moscow State Technical University|Bauman University]] in Moscow. In the same year, he was co-founder of the company ''terraplasma'' in Garching near Munich, which develops devices and processes that use cold plasmas for wound healing, among other things.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.terraplasma.com/ueber-uns/gregor-morfill/|title=Prof. Dr. Dr. h.c. Gregor Morfill – Geschäftsführer • terraplasma GmbH|last=Annika|website=terraplasma GmbH|language=de-DE|access-date=8 March 2020}}</ref>

== Scientific contributions ==
Morfill is the author and co-author of over 500 scientific publications<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Morfill|first1=Gregor E.|last2=Rubin-Zuzic|first2=Milenko|last3=Rothermel|first3=Hermann|last4=Ivlev|first4=Alexei V.|last5=Klumov|first5=Boris A.|last6=Thomas|first6=Hubertus M.|last7=Konopka|first7=Uwe|last8=Steinberg|first8=Victor|date=2004|title=Highly Resolved Fluid Flows: "Liquid Plasmas" at the Kinetic Level|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=92|issue=17|article-number=175004|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.92.175004|pmid=15169161|bibcode=2004PhRvL..92q5004M|issn=0031-9007}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ivlev|first1=A. V.|last2=Morfill|first2=G. E.|last3=Konopka|first3=U.|date=2002|title=Coagulation of Charged Microparticles in Neutral Gas and Charge-Induced Gel Transitions|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=89|issue=19|article-number=195502|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.89.195502|pmid=12443122|bibcode=2002PhRvL..89s5502I|issn=0031-9007}}</ref> and a popular science book on [[chaos theory]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Morfill, Gregor E.|title=Chaos ist überall ... und es funktioniert: eine neue Weltsicht|date=1991|publisher=Ullstein|others=Scheingraber, Herbert.|isbn=3-550-06509-4|location=Frankfurt/Main|oclc=75225038}}</ref>

In addition to his astrophysical work, Gregor Morfill makes important contributions to the subject of "[[Dusty plasma|dusty complex plasmas]]" (with application to [[Astrophysical plasma|space plasmas]] and the explanation of the structure of [[Rings of Saturn|Saturn rings]]), to the discovery of plasma crystals as a solid state of aggregation of dusty plasmas (discovered in 1994)<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Thomas|first1=H.|last2=Morfill|first2=G. E.|last3=Demmel|first3=V.|last4=Goree|first4=J.|last5=Feuerbacher|first5=B.|last6=Möhlmann|first6=D.|date=1994|title=Plasma Crystal: Coulomb Crystallization in a Dusty Plasma|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=73|issue=5|pages=652–655|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.73.652|pmid=10057503|bibcode=1994PhRvL..73..652T|issn=0031-9007}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Rubin-Zuzic|first1=M.|last2=Morfill|first2=G. E.|last3=Ivlev|first3=A. V.|last4=Pompl|first4=R.|last5=Klumov|first5=B. A.|last6=Bunk|first6=W.|last7=Thomas|first7=H. M.|last8=Rothermel|first8=H.|last9=Havnes|first9=O.|last10=Fouquét|first10=A.|date=2006|title=Kinetic development of crystallization fronts in complex plasmas|journal=Nature Physics|volume=2|issue=3|pages=181–185|doi=10.1038/nphys242|bibcode=2006NatPh...2..181R|issn=1745-2473|doi-access=free}}</ref> and to microscopic analysis of the melting process in plasma crystals. He also participates in space plasma experiments with the [[International Space Station]] (ISS), such as the experiment PKE-Nefedov (2001–2005) in cooperation with the [[Russian Space Agency|Russian space agency]] and the Institute for High Energy Densities (IHED, JIHT) in Moscow.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nefedov|first1=Anatoli P.|last2=Morfill|first2=Gregor E.|last3=Fortov|first3=Vladimir E.|last4=Thomas|first4=Hubertus M.|last5=Rothermel|first5=Hermann|last6=Hagl|first6=Tanja|last7=Ivlev|first7=Alexei V.|last8=Zuzic|first8=Milenko|last9=Klumov|first9=Boris A.|last10=Lipaev|first10=Andrey M.|last11=Molotkov|first11=Vladimir I.|date=2003|title=PKE-Nefedov\ast: plasma crystal experiments on the International Space Station|journal=New Journal of Physics|language=en|volume=5|page=33|doi=10.1088/1367-2630/5/1/333|issn=1367-2630|doi-access=free}}</ref> Morfill also researches applications of plasma in medicine such as in the treatment of == Honors and awards ==
* 1998: Bavarian Prime Minister's recognition award
* 1998: {{Interlanguage link|Wissenschaftspreis|lt=|de|Wissenschaftspreis: Forschung zwischen Grundlagen und Anwendungen|WD=}} of the [[Stifterverband für die Deutsche Wissenschaft]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.berlinews.de/archiv/264.shtml|title=Pulsare und Herzflimmern|date=13 October 2007|access-date=8 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071013154027/http://www.berlinews.de/archiv/264.shtml|archive-date=13 October 2007}}</ref>
* 1999: Member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]]
* 2003: Honorary doctorate from the [[Technische Universität Berlin]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.uni-protokolle.de/nachrichten/id/17205/|title=Ehrung für einen Physiker|website=www.uni-protokolle.de|access-date=8 March 2020|archive-date=13 September 2003|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030913112335/http://www.uni-protokolle.de/nachrichten/id/17205/}}</ref>
* 2007: {{Interlanguage link|Ziolkowski Medal|lt=|de|Ziolkowski-Medaille|WD=}} of the Russian space agency [[Roscosmos]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dlr.de/rd/desktopdefault.aspx/tabid-4824/7998_read-9776/7998_page-3/|title=DLR – Raumfahrtmanagement – Deutscher Wissenschaftler erhält höchste Auszeichnung der russischen Raumfahrt-Agentur|website=www.dlr.de|access-date=8 March 2020}}</ref>
* 2010: Fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]]
* 2011: [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] from the [[American Physical Society]] for "''pioneering, and seminal contributions to, the field of [[dusty plasma]]s, including work leading to the discovery of plasma crystals, to an explanation for the complicated structure of [[Rings of Saturn|Saturn's rings]], and to microgravity dusty plasma experiments conducted first on parabolic-trajectory flights and then on the [[International Space Station]].''"<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Morfill&first_nm=Gregor&year=2011|title=2011 James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics Recipient|website=American Physical Society|language=en|access-date=8 March 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mpe.mpg.de/195346/News_20110719|title=James-Maxwell-Preis für Gregor Morfill|website=www.mpe.mpg.de|language=de|access-date=8 March 2020}}</ref>
* Patten Prize<ref name=":0" />
* Gagarin Medal<ref name=":0" />
* URGO Foundation for Advances in Dermatology Award<ref name=":0" />
